sections.heading: Foundations and system components
paragraphs: Modeling and simulation is a problem-based discipline supporting repeated hypothesis testing; its four precepts are modeling, simulation, visualization, and analysis. A system is a collection of interacting or interdependent elements working toward an end, and may be physical (already existing) or notional (a proposed concept). A model represents a system; simulation imitates its behavior over time. The overall M&S process develops a model, executes it, and analyzes output to support decisions.

sections.heading: System structure and boundaries
paragraphs: An entity is an object of interest, an attribute is its property, and an activity causes system changes. The system state describes the entities, attributes, and activities at a point in time. Endogenous activities occur within the system boundary; exogenous activities occur outside it. The slides classify systems with exogenous activities as open, and those without them as closed. Establishing the boundary and identifying entities, attributes, and activities defines model structure; data supplies attribute values and activity relationships.

sections.heading: System behavior and modeling principles
paragraphs: Discrete state variables change at separate instants, whereas continuous state variables change continuously over time. A sampled-data system is intrinsically continuous but observed only at discrete points. Models are useful when direct study is inaccessible, dangerous, unacceptable, or impossible because the system does not yet exist. Block building divides a system into interconnected parts; relevance selects important aspects, accuracy demands correct information, and aggregation combines individual entities into larger ones.

sections.heading: Analytical solutions and simulation
paragraphs: Simple models can sometimes be evaluated analytically using mathematics; numerical simulation can evaluate complex models and gather data to estimate their properties. Simulation facilitates testing alternatives, diagnosing interactions, and identifying bottlenecks without changing the real system. Limitations include the expertise, time, and cost needed to build and interpret models. Simulation is not inherently inexpensive or fast, despite the broad comparison on page 33.

sections.heading: Worked falling-object model and slide correction
paragraphs: With initial height s=1000 ft, initial upward velocity v=100 ft/s, and acceleration -32 ft/s², h(t)=-16t²+100t+1000 and velocity is 100-32t. At t=1 s, h=1084 ft; at t=2 s, h=1136 ft. Page 13's table instead shows 1052 and 972: these do not match the displayed code. The code comment also swaps the meanings of v and s; v is initial velocity and s is initial height.

sections.heading: Model classifications and the development cycle
paragraphs: Models can be static or dynamic, deterministic or stochastic, and continuous or discrete. A deterministic simulation produces a unique output for a specified input; a stochastic simulation uses random inputs and requires statistical analysis of random outputs. The model-code-execute-analyze cycle associates modeling, development, computational, and data/information technologies with the respective phases. Probability and statistics provide random variates for uncertain inputs and methods for analyzing stochastic output.

sections.heading: Simulation approaches
paragraphs: Monte Carlo simulation repeatedly samples input distributions and computes outputs to examine output variability. Continuous simulation represents variables as continuous functions of time and often uses differential equations. Discrete-event simulation changes system variables at distinct event times and advances from one event to the next. These methods differ in their treatment of inputs and time; randomness is not required of every simulation.

sections.heading: Fidelity, resolution, and modeling paradigms
paragraphs: Fidelity describes how closely a model matches reality; low fidelity can be acceptable for aspects unimportant to the study. Resolution or granularity is the level of detail. Physics-based models derive equations from physical principles; finite element modeling decomposes complex objects into smaller elements. Data-based models use data describing the subject; agent-based modeling investigates interacting entities and social phenomena; aggregate modeling combines smaller objects or actions; hybrid modeling combines paradigms.

sections.heading: Simulation participation and applications
paragraphs: Live simulation involves real people operating real systems; virtual simulation involves real people operating simulated systems; constructive simulation uses real inputs that simulated people execute in simulated systems. Training aims at learning, analysis examines system behavior and performance, and experimentation explores solution spaces. Engineering supports design and testing, while acquisition evaluates proposed systems and cost-effectiveness across the system life cycle.

sections.heading: MATLAB basics
paragraphs: MATLAB stands for Matrix Laboratory and supports mathematical computation, visualization, and programming. The workspace displays variables and command history records entered commands. Variable names begin with a letter, may contain letters, digits, and underscores, and are case-sensitive; avoid naming variables after built-in functions. help documents functions, who lists variables, whos provides more details, and clear removes variables. Numeric values default to double; logical values represent true or false.

sections.heading: MATLAB arrays and indexing
paragraphs: An r-by-c matrix has r rows and c columns; a row vector has one row and a column vector has one column. MATLAB indexing starts at 1, and matrix subscripts specify row before column. size returns dimensions, numel counts all elements, and length returns the largest dimension for a matrix. reshape changes dimensions; fliplr reverses columns, flipud reverses rows, rot90 rotates counterclockwise, and repmat tiles copies.

sections.heading: MATLAB calculations and source cautions
paragraphs: For a matrix, sum, prod, min, and max operate down columns by default; specifying dimension 2 operates rowwise. Array multiplication, division, and exponentiation use dotted operators such as .*; matrix multiplication uses * and requires the left column count to equal the right row count. The result has the left matrix’s row count and the right matrix’s column count. Page 88 incorrectly implies sign(0) is -1: it is 0. Page 113 states arrays must be the same size, but compatible sizes can also be implicitly expanded in modern MATLAB. Page 107 overgeneralizes elementwise function behavior: reduction functions such as sum do not preserve the input size.

cards.question: Which four precepts underpin the M&S curriculum in the slides?
cards.correct_answer: Modeling, simulation, visualization, and analysis

cards.question: What distinguishes a notional system from a physical system in the slides?
options: It is a plan or concept for something physical that does not yet exist
It must be a computer program
cards.correct_answer: It is a plan or concept for something physical that does not yet exist

cards.question: What is an entity in system modeling?
options: An object of interest in the system
cards.correct_answer: An object of interest in the system

cards.question: In a factory model, what is a property of a machine called?
cards.correct_answer: An attribute

cards.question: What is the role of an activity in the slides’ system terminology?
options: It is a process that causes system changes
It is a property of an entity
It is always external to the system
cards.correct_answer: It is a process that causes system changes

cards.question: An activity occurring outside the chosen system boundary is called what?
cards.correct_answer: Exogenous

cards.question: What defines a sampled-data system?
options: It is intrinsically continuous but information is available at discrete times
Its state changes only at events
cards.correct_answer: It is intrinsically continuous but information is available at discrete times

cards.question: Which is a reason to model rather than directly engage a system?
options: The system may be dangerous or may not yet exist
cards.correct_answer: The system may be dangerous or may not yet exist

cards.question: What belongs to establishing a model structure?
options: Determining the boundary and identifying entities, attributes, and activities
Executing a model before identifying its boundary
cards.correct_answer: Determining the boundary and identifying entities, attributes, and activities

cards.question: What does the relevance principle recommend?
options: Include only aspects relevant to the investigation
cards.correct_answer: Include only aspects relevant to the investigation

cards.question: What does aggregation do in modeling?
options: Groups individual entities into larger entities
cards.correct_answer: Groups individual entities into larger entities

cards.question: When can an analytical solution be useful?
options: When the model is simple enough for mathematical methods to yield the desired information
Only when all system behavior is random
Only when the actual system is inaccessible
cards.correct_answer: When the model is simple enough for mathematical methods to yield the desired information

cards.question: Which is an advantage of simulation described in the slides?
options: Testing changes and policies without affecting the real system
Removing the need for domain expertise
cards.correct_answer: Testing changes and policies without affecting the real system

cards.question: Which limitation of simulation is identified in the slides?
options: Model development and interpretation can require expertise, time, and expense
cards.correct_answer: Model development and interpretation can require expertise, time, and expense

cards.question: Which sequence describes the M&S development cycle presented?
cards.correct_answer: Model, code, execute, analyze

cards.question: What makes a simulation deterministic?
options: A given input set produces a unique determined output
The system necessarily advances by events
cards.correct_answer: A given input set produces a unique determined output

cards.question: Why are statistical techniques important for stochastic simulation?
options: Random inputs produce random outputs that need analysis
They guarantee a single output for every input distribution
cards.correct_answer: Random inputs produce random outputs that need analysis

cards.question: What is the central procedure in Monte Carlo simulation?
options: Repeatedly sample input distributions and calculate outputs
Advance exclusively from one event to the next
Solve only a single differential equation analytically
Operate real equipment with real people
cards.correct_answer: Repeatedly sample input distributions and calculate outputs

cards.question: Which model type commonly uses differential equations for variables evolving with time?
cards.correct_answer: Continuous simulation

cards.question: How does a discrete-event simulation advance time?
options: From one event to the next
Only backward from the final state
cards.correct_answer: From one event to the next

cards.question: What does fidelity describe?
options: How closely a model or simulation matches reality
The number of rows in a matrix
The duration of a simulation run
cards.correct_answer: How closely a model or simulation matches reality

cards.question: What does higher resolution mean in the slides?
options: More detail is included in the simulation
The simulation necessarily matches reality perfectly
The simulation has no random input
cards.correct_answer: More detail is included in the simulation

cards.question: What is the basic idea of finite element modeling?
options: Decompose a complicated object into small elements and model them
Replace all physical laws with random numbers
Require real people to operate real systems
cards.correct_answer: Decompose a complicated object into small elements and model them

cards.question: Which approach combines more than one modeling paradigm?
cards.correct_answer: Hybrid modeling

cards.question: Which participation category involves real people operating simulated systems?
cards.correct_answer: Virtual simulation

cards.question: How is constructive simulation characterized in the slides?
options: Real people provide inputs executed by simulated people in simulated systems
Only physical models can be used
cards.correct_answer: Real people provide inputs executed by simulated people in simulated systems

cards.question: What is the main intent of a training application?
cards.correct_answer: Produce learning in the participant

cards.question: What is an acquisition application intended to evaluate before committing funds?
options: Cost-effectiveness and correctness of a proposed system
Only the color of visualization graphics
Only the length of a MATLAB vector
Whether all physical systems are continuous
cards.correct_answer: Cost-effectiveness and correctness of a proposed system

cards.question: What does MATLAB stand for?
cards.correct_answer: Matrix Laboratory

cards.question: Which MATLAB command displays more detail about workspace variables?
cards.correct_answer: whos

cards.question: Which is a valid MATLAB variable name under the slide rules?
cards.correct_answer: value_1

cards.question: What is the default MATLAB numeric type described in the slides?
cards.correct_answer: double

cards.question: What are the dimensions of a column vector with five elements?
cards.correct_answer: 5 by 1

cards.question: In MATLAB, which expression addresses row 2, column 3 of matrix A?
For a 2-by-3 matrix, what does numel return?
Which function reverses matrix columns from left to right?
cards.correct_answer: fliplr

cards.question: What does repmat(A,2,3) construct?
options: A 2-by-3 arrangement of copies of A
A matrix with exactly 2 rows and 3 columns regardless of A
The second and third elements of A
cards.correct_answer: A 2-by-3 arrangement of copies of A

cards.question: For an r-by-c matrix, what is the shape of sum(A) using the default dimension?
cards.correct_answer: 1 by c

cards.question: Which MATLAB operation multiplies corresponding array elements?
cards.correct_answer: A .* B

cards.question: If A is 2-by-3 and B is 3-by-4, what is the size of A * B?
cards.correct_answer: 2 by 4

cards.question: Which MATLAB function calculates the determinant of square matrix A?
cards.correct_answer: det(A)

cards.question: Which function returns the natural logarithm of x in MATLAB?
cards.correct_answer: log(x)
